sections.title: Form and cultivation
sections.text: Arachis hypogaea, the peanut or groundnut, is a low annual legume, generally about 20–60 cm tall. After flowering, its stalk elongates and pushes the developing pod underground; pods usually contain one to four seeds. It originated as a cultigen in Bolivia and is now grown widely in warm regions.

sections.title: Food and allergy
sections.text: The seeds are eaten fresh, roasted or boiled, or pressed for oil; pods are botanical fruits, not true nuts. Peanut is a major food allergen and can cause severe reactions in sensitized people.
